items.prompt: Bu ilacı aç karnına içmeyin, zira mideyi bozar. — zira introduces…
items.say: Bu ilacı aç karnına içmeyin, zira mideyi bozar.
items.explanation: After zira comes the reason: the medicine upsets your stomach.

items.prompt: Ceketini al, aksi hâlde üşürsün. — aksi hâlde introduces…
items.explanation: Aksi hâlde means “otherwise.” Skip the jacket and you'll freeze.

items.prompt: Açıkçası, bu film hiç hoşuma gitmedi. — açıkçası means…
items.say: Açıkçası, bu film hiç hoşuma gitmedi.
items.explanation: Açıkçası with the -sı tail means “to be honest.” “Clearly” is açıkça.

items.prompt: Which connector sounds bookish, like a conference talk?
items.explanation: Zira is the bookish brother of çünkü. Yoksa is the most casual “or else.”

entries.text: Formu bugün doldurun, ___ başvurunuz geçersiz olur.

items.explanation: A reason after the gap means zira. Trouble if you don't do it means aksi hâlde. An honest opinion at the start means açıkçası.

exercises.instruction: Match the beginning and the ending

items.explanation: Advice or “have to” pulls in aksi hâlde and trouble. A fact pulls in zira and a reason. Açıkçası just squeezes into an opinion.

exercises.instruction: Build it, find the mistake, say it yourself

items.translation: We have to leave early, otherwise we'll get stuck in traffic.
items.explanation: First “have to leave” with -malı, then aksi hâlde, then trouble: trafiğe kalırız.
“It was cold” is a reason, not trouble. Reasons come with zira.
“Otherwise” in the sense of “differently” is farklı. Aksi hâlde doesn't fit here.

items.translation: To be honest, I really liked Samsun.
items.explanation: “To be honest” is açıkçası, with the -sı tail.

exercises.instruction: Phrase prescription: pick the right drug
exercises.description: A sentence with a gap and three connector capsules: zira, aksi hâlde, açıkçası. The capsule flies into the gap along an arc. Keys 1–3. Logic lives in index.html.

items.ctx: You explain why you took an umbrella.
items.ru: I took an umbrella, for it was cloudy.
items.explanation: Cloudy is the reason. Reasons come with zira.

items.ctx: You warn a friend at the tram stop in Atakum.
items.full: Kartına para yükle, aksi hâlde tramvaya binemezsin.
items.ru: Top up your card, otherwise you won't get on the tram.
items.explanation: Advice first, trouble second. That's aksi hâlde's job.

items.ctx: You try the pide and decide not to lie.
items.ru: To be honest, this pide is a bit salty.
items.explanation: At the start, before an honest opinion: açıkçası.

items.ctx: You write a formal email to your colleagues.
items.ru: The meeting was moved, for the director fell ill.
items.explanation: The director fell ill: that's the reason. Formal tone: zira.

items.ctx: You talk your roommate into going to bed early.
items.full: Erken yatmalısın, aksi hâlde sabah uyanamazsın.
items.ru: You need to go to bed early, otherwise you won't wake up in the morning.
items.explanation: “Need to” with -malı and trouble after it: aksi hâlde.

items.ctx: Your boss asks what you think of the new plan.
items.ru: To be honest, I didn't like this plan at all.
items.explanation: A bold opinion opens with açıkçası.

items.prompt: How do you say “I think otherwise”?
items.explanation: “Otherwise” = “differently” → farklı. Aksi hâlde threatens a consequence.

items.statement: “Hava soğuktu, zira ceket giydim”: the order is right.
items.explanation: After zira comes the reason: Ceket giydim, zira hava soğuktu.

items.translation: We need to book a table in advance, otherwise we won't find a seat.
items.explanation: First “need to,” then trouble: aksi hâlde.

items.prompt: Doktor durumu açıkça anlattı. — açıkça means…
items.explanation: Without the -sı tail, açıkça means “clearly, openly.” “To be honest” is açıkçası.
This one means “on the contrary,” and that's aksine.
